projects.title: Unveiling the Black Box: Evaluating XAI Techniques LIME, Grad-CAM, and Integrated Gradients for CNN Explainability
projects.description:
Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) aims to enhance the transparency and trustworthiness of complex machine learning models, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This study evaluates three XAI techniques—LIME, Grad-CAM, and Integrated Gradients (IG)—to understand their effectiveness in explaining the decisions made by a CNN model.

A 2D CNN was trained on the TF-Flowers dataset using Python. The dataset comprises photos classified into several flower types. The CNN architecture was specifically designed to capture and classify relevant visual elements in the dataset. The XAI techniques were applied to elucidate the CNN model's decision-making process, providing insights into how shapes and patterns influence predictions.

The CNN achieved 75.3% accuracy on the TF-Flowers dataset. LIME highlighted local feature importance by altering input features, Grad-CAM emphasized crucial regions like petal structures, and Integrated Gradients showcased feature importance by revealing significant contributions from color gradients and texture patterns. Grad-CAM effectively identified distinct botanical patterns, while LIME and IG offered additional insights into fine-scale characteristics and pixel-level attributions.

The present research shows how CNN decision-making on complex datasets like TF-Flowers may be explained by XAI approaches like LIME, Grad-CAM, and Integrated Gradients. Transparency and interpretability are increased by each technique's distinct insights into model predictions. Combining these techniques provides a more comprehensive understanding of model behavior, which is essential for creating reliable AI systems for real-world applications.

projects.title: Sign Me In
projects.description: Undertook the development of a web-based application for Florence Darlington Technical College's Math Hub with a partner. The application aims at improving the student sign-in process for those seeking tutoring or examination services at the Math Hub. The project's primary focus is streamlining student sign-ins, while also providing management tools to assess the Math Hub's performance through detailed reports and data visualization. This endeavor involves a range of technologies, including HTML with Razor syntax, CSS, Bootstrap for the frontend, and C# in conjunction with the .NET framework (specifically, Blazor Server) for the robust backend. Data was securely managed using an Azure SQL database with Entity Framework integration, and we followed Scrum and Agile methodologies.
